title: Brock Bowers Set to Return Next Week, NBC Sports Confirms He’s “Good to Go”
body:
The Oakland Raiders will likely have their starting tight end back on the field next week after a brief, ankle‑related setback on Sunday. Brock Bowers, who was limited to just 11 snaps before exiting the contest against the Seattle Seahawks, is expected to be cleared for practice and game action by the time the team faces the Denver Broncos in the upcoming Thursday night matchup.

Bowers’ injury was not a surprise to the Raiders’ medical staff, who had been monitoring a lingering ankle issue that had flared up during the first half of the Seahawks game. The 22‑year‑old rookie, who was drafted in the second round and quickly emerged as a reliable target in the passing game, suffered a mild sprain after a hard tackle on a third‑down conversion. He was helped off the field by trainers and did not return for the remainder of the contest, which the Raiders ultimately lost 24‑17.

While the loss itself was disappointing, Bowers’ limited involvement highlighted a growing concern for Oakland’s offensive scheme. The tight end has become a pivotal piece in head coach Josh McDaniels’ play‑calling, often lining up in the slot or on the line of scrimmage to create mismatches against slower linebackers or undersized defensive backs. In the first three games of the season, Bowers has recorded 23 receptions for 215 yards and two touchdowns, ranking him among the top rookie tight ends in the league. His ability to gain separation and secure contested catches has allowed the Raiders to diversify their attack beyond the traditional run‑heavy approach that characterized the team in previous years.

The medical evaluation conducted on Sunday night indicated that the sprain is classified as a Grade I injury, which typically requires a short period of rest, ice, compression and elevation, followed by a gradual return to activity. Raiders’ head athletic trainer Jeff Kline confirmed that Bowers has responded well to treatment and is progressing through the rehabilitation protocol without any setbacks. “We’re optimistic,” Kline said in a brief interview. “He’s been diligent with his rehab, and there’s no indication that this will linger beyond the next few days.” The team’s internal timeline suggests that Bowers could participate in the full practice session on Wednesday, giving him ample opportunity to re‑establish timing with quarterback Derek Carr before the Thursday night game.

The timing of Bowers’ return could prove crucial for Oakland’s offensive rhythm. The Raiders have struggled to generate consistent third‑down conversions, converting just 31 percent of attempts through the first three weeks. Bowers’ presence on the field provides a safety valve for Carr, especially in short‑yardage situations where the defense often stacks the box. Moreover, his versatility allows the Raiders to employ more two‑tight‑end sets, a formation that has been effective for teams like the New England Patriots and the Kansas City Chiefs in creating unpredictable passing angles. If Bowers is fully cleared, the Raiders could see an uptick in red‑zone efficiency, an area where they have been notably inefficient, scoring only two touchdowns in the red zone over the past three games.

Looking ahead, the Broncos present a favorable matchup for the Raiders’ rejuvenated offense. Denver’s secondary has struggled against tight ends this season, allowing a 45.6% completion rate when targeted in the intermediate range. Should Bowers return to full health, Oakland will likely look to exploit that weakness, incorporating him into play designs that emphasize seam routes and crossing patterns across the middle of the field. The coaching staff has hinted at a “tight‑end‑centric” game plan in the coming weeks, a strategic shift that could elevate the Raiders’ offensive ceiling and relieve some of the pressure on Carr, who has been under scrutiny for his decision‑making.

In sum, Brock Bowers’ anticipated clearance marks a positive development for a Raiders squad seeking to find its identity early in the season. The tight end’s skill set not only broadens the playbook but also provides a reliable option in critical moments. If the medical staff’s optimistic outlook holds true, Oakland will enter Thursday night’s contest with a more complete offensive arsenal, positioning itself to rebound from the recent defeat and build momentum as the season progresses.
